newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent hovers just above $18 but products weigh.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent hovers just above $18 but products weigh.

text.p: IPE Brent held just above the psychologically important $18 a barrel mark on Wednesday afternoon but oil products were beginning to exert downward pressure.
Dealers said the market was dragged lower, after a firm start, by sluggish gas oil and poor demand for other oil products in Europe such as gasoline and heavy fuel.
June Brent was up six cents a barrel at $18.05 at 1515 GMT after bouncing off $18.00 a few minutes earlier. Prices hit a peak of $18.19 soon after the open but slid steadily lower during the day.
Brokers MeesPierson Derivatives pegged support at $17.80 and others saw additional support at $17.65, the nine-month low hit earlier this month.
Physical Brent was under pressure from CFDs swaps, which slipped slightly, but dealers said news of a resumption of oil loading at Nigeria's Bonny terminal had little market impact.
Prices had firmed earlier after the release of weekly data from the American Petroleum Institute (API) which traders construed as being mildly bullish.
Meanwhile, the gas oil contract was down 25 cents a tonne at $163.50 on June at 1511 GMT, having been flat or slightly firmer for most of the day.
Dealers said the physical market was slow with premiums versus the IPE unchanged.
